title: Graph Beta: establish Foundation attempt input authority
description: Graph Beta prerequisite for task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038. Resolve, then land, the production authority source for the Foundation dispatch request’s launchTemplate and inputManifest instead of accepting an accidental caller copy. At planning time record the per-field decision “server-derived/durable” versus “caller-proposed but bounded and authenticated” for argv, cwd, environment, bootstrap credential digest, launch selection, limits, runtime observation, base identity, and workspace entries; unresolved fields block rather than default. Measurement at HEAD a42ae2f1f9168d13b8b786404fc47b366cc8edd9: FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_KEYS requires launchTemplate/inputManifest; packages/runner exports builders and workspace observers, but daemon production has no launch-template producer and its only durable inputManifest reader belongs to the separate sealed foundation-verification aggregate. This task creates the lawful production source/hydration seam. Stage: GRAPH BETA. Not in scope: attempt command registration, current-graph projection, claim/activation, provider dispatch internals, widening effect.activate, or editing the authoritative design.
definitionOfDone: Planning notes record a complete per-field authority matrix for launchTemplate and inputManifest, including why each field is server-derived/durable or caller-proposed; no field is left implicit, and any caller-proposed field has an exact authenticated payload allow-list and bound.

A focused production source/hydrator produces the exact FoundationAttemptLaunchTemplate and WorkspaceInputManifest for a project/session/node using approved durable facts and real runner/host observation surfaces; it never accepts caller-selected grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect, or process-registration authority.

Workspace input is sealed through the production @moe/runner manifest builder against the observed base identity and actual bounded entries, while runtime/launch facts remain tied to server-owned provider capabilities; mismatched base, stale observation, missing workspace, hostile path/argv/environment, or unverifiable runtime fails closed with an exact stable code and layer.

Repeated reads of the same durable identity are byte-stable; conflicting durable/caller-proposed bytes refuse before claim, activation, launch, or process registration and leave zero durable/provider residue.

Focused tests exercise the production source with real durable store and filesystem/host seams, assert exact reason code and layer plus nonzero generated hostile-case counts, include one accepted control, and cover Windows path/argv behavior plus platform-neutral macOS/Linux rejection semantics without shell-normalizing authority.

Completion names task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038 as the production consumer and records the exact call-site/dependency edge; daemon typecheck/test and plain-Node provider construction execute with nonzero test evidence.
taskRails: The server-derived versus caller-proposed choice is a Graph Beta authority decision; do not infer it from the existing caller-shaped FoundationAttemptDispatchRequest or silently broaden effect.activate.
Reuse public @moe/runner roots and existing durable/session/provider facts; do not reimplement workspace sealing, runtime observation, or launch selection in daemon tests.
Keep this source/hydration seam separate from Foundation ingress, graph projection, activation, and launch execution.
Fail closed with stable reason codes/layers, use TDD, target <=250 lines per production source and split before 400, preserve foreign work, and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE (read-only). The governor's SPLIT is executed: Half B was filed as task-9a1eb61d566e47838c9f79c030da1f70 during planning, so THIS task is the INPUT-MANIFEST half only. Do not touch argv, launchSelection or limits — they belong to that task.
Step 1 of the original plan is complete and green (worker-a83aecdf); its evidence stands and is not repeated. Re-confirm only what this half stands on, at current HEAD:
(a) PRODUCERS PRESENT: `grep -n 'buildInputManifest\|observeScope\|createNodeGitObserver\|createNodeScopePaths\|WorkspaceInputManifest' packages/runner/src/index.ts` -> :55 createNodeGitObserver, :56 createNodeScopePaths, :59 observeScope, :274 WorkspaceInputManifest, :279 buildInputManifest. All five reachable from the BARE root.
(b) DEPENDENCY EDGE already proven on all three legs by step 1 and unchanged: apps/daemon declares @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler, pnpm-lock carries both apps/daemon importer links, and a compiled bare-specifier probe typechecked clean. Re-run the probe only — write it, `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, EXIT=0, delete in the same command.
(c) DO NOT CONCLUDE A RUNTIME SURFACE IS MISSING BY GREPPING packages/runner/src/index.ts. `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` (claude-host-runtime.ts:201) and `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` reach the bare root through NESTED `export *` (index.ts -> surface/claude-surface.js -> claude-discovery-surface.js). A direct grep of index.ts misses them — worker-a83aecdf recorded this trap explicitly.
(d) THE GAP IS OPEN AND ITS SHAPE IS THE POINT: foundation-attempt-service.ts:173-177 currently calls `buildInputManifest({baseIdentity: request.inputManifest.baseIdentity, entries: request.inputManifest.entries as never})` — it SEALS THE CALLER'S OWN ENTRIES. That is the accidental caller copy this task replaces. Confirm it still reads that way.
(e) THE PRE-EXISTING FOREIGN RED, recorded by step 1 and to be re-measured rather than assumed: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` was exiting 1 purely on other agents' uncommitted work in src/goals/goal-services.test.ts and src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts. Capture the baseline failing-path set BEFORE editing anything; it must stay disjoint from this task's owned paths, and you may not repair it.

RECORD THE PER-FIELD AUTHORITY MATRIX for the INPUT MANIFEST — DoD 1, narrowed to this half by the split. Write it into the module header of the hydrator you create in step 4, not only into a completion note, so a later reader cannot re-open a settled question.
`FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_INPUT_KEYS` is exactly `["baseIdentity", "entries"]` (foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:90) and `WorkspaceInputManifest` is `{manifestVersion, baseIdentity, entries, sha256}` (workspace-contract.ts:66-71). Decide and record BOTH rows:
- **baseIdentity** — SERVER-OBSERVED. It is the git HEAD the daemon itself observes through `createNodeGitObserver(...).headCommit()`. A caller may PROPOSE one, but `observeScope` already refuses a mismatch with `RUNNER_SCOPE_HEAD_MISMATCH` (scope-observation.ts:129-133), so the caller's value is used for agreement and never as the source.
- **entries** — SERVER-OBSERVED, and this is the row that closes the gap. Today the request's entries are sealed verbatim; after this task the daemon observes the workspace and produces them.
STATE THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, because it is the shape of the work: `observeScope` returns `ScopeCanonicalEntry` = `{path, attribution, attributionReason}` (scope-contract.ts:143-147) and `ScopePathObserver` is `{realpath, exists}` (:76-79). NEITHER carries `sha256` or `byteLength`, which `WorkspaceInputEntry` requires (workspace-contract.ts:59-64). So the hydrator must read each observed path's bytes and compute its digest and length itself. That is OBSERVATION, not authority — the SEALING stays with `buildInputManifest`, per task rail 2. Say so explicitly in the header so nobody later mistakes the hashing for a second manifest builder.
- **producer** — `WorkspaceProducer` is `{kind:"BASE"}` or `{kind:"PREDECESSOR", attemptRef, epoch, adoptionRef?}` (workspace-contract.ts:50-57), and its own comment says producer identity is mandatory because "a content digest is one-way, so nothing downstream can ask 'which attempt produced these bytes' unless the input manifest already says". Decide where PREDECESSOR facts come from; if no durable predecessor source exists for this slice, record BASE-only as the decision and its bound, and say why — an unresolved field blocks rather than defaults.

TESTS FIRST. Create apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-input-hydrator.test.ts against REAL seams — a real temp git worktree (`mkdtempSync`, `git init`, one commit) driven through `createNodeGitObserver` and `createNodeScopePaths`, and a real filesystem for the content reads. Task rail 2 forbids reimplementing workspace sealing or scope observation in daemon tests, so drive the production observers rather than fakes for the accepted control.
Write RED, the accepted control first: for a temp repository with two committed files under a declared scope path, the hydrator returns a sealed `WorkspaceInputManifest` whose `baseIdentity` equals the repository's real HEAD and whose `entries` carry the true `sha256` and `byteLength` of those files.
ASSERT AGAINST THE PRODUCTION SURFACE, not against hand-written hex: compute the expected digest with the same `node:crypto` call the hydrator uses over bytes read in the test, and assert the manifest's own `sha256` equals `buildInputManifest(...)`'s output for those entries. A test with both operands hand-written is a tautology; a test that hard-codes a digest silently pins today's file content.
Also assert the hydrator's answer is deeply frozen and that repeated calls over unchanged bytes are byte-stable (DoD 4's first half).
Confirm the suite fails because the module does not exist — not because the git fixture is wrong. A temp repo that fails to init makes every later assertion vacuous.

Land the hydrator: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-input-hydrator.ts plus its EXACT one-line LF bridge `export * from "./foundation-input-hydrator.ts";` (a new .ts without its bridge is invisible to consumers while tsc and vitest both stay green).
`hydrateFoundationInputManifest({worktreeRoot, declaredScopePaths, observedAt, gitObserver, pathObserver, ...})`, in this order:
1. OBSERVE, do not accept: call `observeScope({worktreeRoot, baseIdentity, declaredScopePaths, gitObserver, pathObserver, observedAt, observerVersion})`. The `baseIdentity` passed in is the caller's PROPOSAL and `observeScope` refuses a mismatch against the real HEAD with `RUNNER_SCOPE_HEAD_MISMATCH` — forward that code and the runner's scope layer VERBATIM, never restamped.
2. For each `observation.canonicalEntries` path, read the file's bytes under an explicit byte ceiling and compute `sha256` and `byteLength`. Refuse with an exact local code on an unreadable path, a path that vanished between observation and read, or a file over the ceiling. A path present in the observation but absent on disk is a STALE OBSERVATION and must fail closed — DoD 3 names it.
3. Attach `producer` per the step-2 decision.
4. SEAL through the production builder: `buildInputManifest({baseIdentity: observation.baseIdentity, entries})` — note `observation.baseIdentity`, the OBSERVED value, never the proposal. Forward its refusal code with the runner workspace layer, exactly as foundation-attempt-service.ts:178 already does.
5. Return the sealed manifest plus the observation it was sealed against, deeply frozen.
NOTHING HERE MAY ACCEPT AUTHORITY: no grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect or process registration — the contracts file's own comment at :91-96 calls the request shape "AUTHORITY-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION" and this producer must stay that way. Keep the file at or under 250 physical lines; if the content-reading loop pushes it over, split the read-and-digest helper into a sibling module with its own exact one-line LF bridge and record the measured count as the forcing evidence.

THE CALLER-CANNOT-WIN MATRIX — the heart of this task, since the whole point is replacing an accidental caller copy. Every case asserts the exact code AND the refusing layer, because three layers can answer here (the runner's scope layer, the runner's workspace layer, and this module's own) and a test asserting only `ok === false` would stay green if one started swallowing another.
- BASE MISMATCH: a proposed `baseIdentity` that is not the repository's real HEAD -> `RUNNER_SCOPE_HEAD_MISMATCH` at the RUNNER's scope layer, not a daemon code.
- CALLER ENTRIES ARE IGNORED, asserted positively: pass a set of caller-proposed entries that CONTRADICT what is on disk — wrong digests, wrong lengths, an extra path that does not exist — and assert the sealed manifest carries the OBSERVED entries instead. This is the assertion that proves the copy was replaced rather than merely wrapped, and it is the one a reviewer should look for first.
- STALE OBSERVATION: delete a file between observation and read -> fail closed with the exact code, no partial manifest.
- MISSING WORKSPACE: a `worktreeRoot` that does not exist, and separately one that is not a git repository -> distinct refusals, both fail-closed.
- HOSTILE PATHS: absolute paths, `..` traversal, a symlink escaping the worktree, a NUL byte, a non-NFC path, and a path over the length bound. `observeScope` canonicalizes and `buildInputManifest` refuses non-canonical paths with `RUNNER_WORKSPACE_PATH_NOT_CANONICAL` — assert which layer refuses each, and do NOT shell-normalize anything before handing it over (DoD 5 says so in terms).
- ENTRY LIMIT: over `MAX_WORKSPACE_ENTRIES` -> `RUNNER_WORKSPACE_ENTRY_LIMIT` at the workspace layer.
- GENERATED HOSTILE SWEEP over the input record. Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing — and assert each refuses rather than throwing. A crash is not a refusal.

WINDOWS AND CROSS-PLATFORM SEMANTICS — DoD 5, and it is a first-class requirement here rather than a caveat, because this module touches the filesystem and git.
- WINDOWS PATHS: a path containing a space, one containing a backslash separator, and a drive-letter absolute path. Assert the refusal or canonicalization is the runner's, not a daemon-side rewrite — DoD 5 forbids shell-normalizing authority, so the daemon must hand paths over as observed and let `buildInputManifest` judge canonicality.
- CASE SENSITIVITY: two paths differing only in case. On Windows they may collide on disk while remaining distinct strings; assert whichever layer refuses does so with an exact code rather than silently deduplicating, since a silently dropped entry is an input nobody sealed.
- LINE ENDINGS: a file with CRLF content. Its `byteLength` and `sha256` must be over the RAW bytes; a text-mode read would change both and silently alter the manifest identity. Assert the digest matches a raw-bytes read.
- PLATFORM-NEUTRAL REJECTION: the macOS/Linux semantics must be exercised as REJECTION cases that hold on any platform — do not `skip` them off-Windows, or the suite proves nothing where it actually runs. Where a case genuinely cannot be constructed on the current platform, assert the constructor refused rather than skipping silently.
- Close every handle and remove every temp worktree in a `finally` on every exit path; a leaked git process or open handle surfaces as an unrelated-looking worker crash.

BYTE-STABILITY AND ZERO RESIDUE — DoD 4.
- REPEATED READS ARE BYTE-STABLE: hydrate the same unchanged worktree twice and assert the two sealed manifests serialize identically, including `sha256` and entry order. `buildInputManifest` orders entries itself; assert the order is derived rather than incidental by presenting the same files in a different declared-scope order and getting the same manifest.
- CONFLICTING BYTES REFUSE BEFORE ANY DOWNSTREAM EFFECT: this hydrator runs BEFORE claim, activation, launch and process registration, so the strongest available assertion is that it performs no durable write and starts no process. Drive it with a real store handle in scope and assert raw event and command-decision counts are unchanged, and that no child process was spawned beyond the git observer's own reads.
- ZERO RESIDUE: after every refusal arm, assert no temp file, no lock and no partial manifest was left behind, and that the worktree's own files are untouched — capture a before/after inventory of digest, size and mtime for the fixture files. mtime matters: a read that accidentally opened for write restores identical content but moves it, and that is the only signal.
- Run the suite TWICE in one command; a teardown that has only ever run once has not been tested, and this suite creates git worktrees on every case.

MUTATION DRILLS against the production surface. Run each, record the exact test name that reddened, restore, and confirm the restored bytes hash-match the original — git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree, where a foreign hook commit can swallow a drill.
1. THE CALLER-ECHO DRILL, and it is the one this whole task exists to prevent: make the hydrator seal `input.entries` (the caller's) instead of the observed entries. The caller-entries-ignored test must redden. If it stays green, the accidental copy is still in place wearing a new name — precisely the failure worker-a83aecdf warned about and the governor's split was made to isolate.
2. Seal against the PROPOSED `baseIdentity` instead of `observation.baseIdentity`. A named test must redden; note that with a matching proposal the two are equal, so the drill only bites if a case deliberately proposes a mismatching base — confirm such a case exists.
3. Skip a path that vanished between observation and read instead of refusing. The stale-observation test must redden — a silently omitted entry is an input nobody sealed, which is the same class of defect as a silently dropped effect.
4. Restamp a runner refusal into a local daemon code. The base-mismatch test must redden ON THE LAYER, not just the code.
5. Read file content as text instead of raw bytes. The CRLF digest test must redden.
If a drill survives, do not rationalise it: either the assertion has detached from its subject or the mutation is equivalent. Say which, with evidence.

GATE, with the foreign-red baseline handled explicitly — this is the step most likely to produce a false completion claim on this task.
Run exactly:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; A=$?; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; B=$?; echo "TC=$A TEST=$B"`
Exit codes captured separately — no pipes (a piped run reports the pipe tail's code) and no `&&` chaining (a red typecheck then hides the count line). READ THE OUTPUT: the test leg must print a `Test Files N passed` count line with a NONZERO count; exit 0 with no count line is UNVERIFIED. @moe/daemon resolves to apps/daemon.
THE TYPECHECK LEG MAY EXIT 1 ON WORK THAT IS NOT YOURS. Step 1(e) captured the baseline failing-path set at the merge-base; capture it again at HEAD and compute the delta. Completion is permitted only when the delta intersected with this task's owned paths (apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-input-hydrator.*) is EMPTY. Report the foreign red VERBATIM with its exact failing lines and file paths — disclosed, never hidden, never fabricated green — and do not attempt to repair another agent's files.
Do NOT use that allowance to excuse a red your own diff caused: the (2)-minus-(1) delta is precisely what detects it.
DoD 6 ALSO REQUIRES PLAIN-NODE PROVIDER CONSTRUCTION, which vitest cannot prove — it rewrites `./foo.js` back to `foo.ts` and aliases workspace packages, so a missing or malformed `.js` bridge passes the entire suite. Load the new bridge in a REAL child process (`node --input-type=module -e 'await import("<abs path>/foundation-input-hydrator.js")'`) and require exit 0. Record the command and its output.
Re-measure `wc -l` on the new production file(s) and record it.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker:
- Can ANY caller-supplied value reach the sealed manifest as a FACT rather than as a proposal checked for agreement? Trace `baseIdentity` and every entry field to its observed source.
- Does the hydrator accept a grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect or process registration on any path? The contracts file calls the request shape authority-free by construction; confirm this producer is too.
- Is any runner refusal restamped or flattened? Both the scope layer and the workspace layer must survive verbatim.
- Did anything write, spawn, or leave residue? Re-check the before/after fixture inventory including mtime.
- Confirm each production file is at or under 250 physical lines, each has its exact one-line LF `.js` bridge, the step-1 probe is deleted, and `git status --porcelain` shows only owned paths.
COMPLETION MUST RECORD:
1. THE SPLIT: this task is Half A (input manifest) of the governor's decision in comment-cf245bba; Half B is task-9a1eb61d566e47838c9f79c030da1f70 (server-owned launch-template producers for argv, launchSelection and limits), filed during planning. The shared consumer task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038 needs BOTH halves — this landing does not clear its path on its own, and saying otherwise would misreport readiness for task-203a5ca7 and task-933605a5.
2. THE CONSUMER EDGE per DoD 6: name `hydrateFoundationInputManifest(...)` from apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-input-hydrator.js and state that foundation-attempt-service.ts:173-177 is the call site that should stop sealing `request.inputManifest.entries` — whether that rewiring lands here or in the consumer task, say which, explicitly.
3. The per-field authority matrix from step 2, and which drills reddened which named tests.
4. The foreign-red baseline and the empty owned-path delta, verbatim.
Commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC only — `git commit -- <path> ...` — never a bare `git commit`, per this epic's rail 3: the index is shared state and a bare commit captures another task's staged files. Verify with `git show --stat` that only owned paths landed.

1) PLAN BOTH HALVES IN ONE TASK, as the original 8-step plan did. REJECTED by the governor's explicit SPLIT decision (comment-cf245bba, standing authority) and by measurement: argv, launchSelection and limits have NO server-owned producer at HEAD, so planning them here would force either a narrowed DoD or a bounded type filled from the request — a caller echo wearing a server-derived label, green suite and all. Filed as task-9a1eb61d566e47838c9f79c030da1f70 during this planning session.
2) DECLARE BOUNDED TYPES FOR THE THREE UNSOURCED FIELDS and call the authority question closed. REJECTED, and this is the trap worker-a83aecdf named precisely: "A bounded SHAPE is trivially constructible — which is exactly what makes this dangerous. Declaring a type does not create a source." A `validate*()` over a request field is not a reader.
3) KEEP SEALING THE CALLER'S ENTRIES and merely validate them harder. REJECTED: that is the accidental caller copy the task exists to replace. foundation-attempt-service.ts:173-177 seals `request.inputManifest.entries` verbatim today; validation of a caller's digest cannot tell you what is actually on disk.
4) REIMPLEMENT SEALING OR SCOPE OBSERVATION IN THE DAEMON. REJECTED by task rail 2. `buildInputManifest` stays the only sealer and `observeScope` the only scope observer; the daemon's new work is strictly the content read between them.
5) DERIVE ENTRY DIGESTS FROM `observeScope` ALONE. IMPOSSIBLE, and it shapes the whole design: `ScopeCanonicalEntry` is `{path, attribution, attributionReason}` and `ScopePathObserver` is `{realpath, exists}` — neither carries `sha256` or `byteLength`, which `WorkspaceInputEntry` requires. The daemon must read the bytes itself. That is observation, not authority, and the header must say so or a later reader will mistake it for a second manifest builder.
6) USE FAKE GIT/PATH OBSERVERS FOR THE ACCEPTED CONTROL, as apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-closure-test-fixtures.ts:194 does. REJECTED for the control: task rail 2 forbids reimplementing observation in daemon tests, and DoD 5 requires real filesystem/host seams. Fakes remain appropriate for specific hostile arms that cannot be constructed on disk.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD f96995d8. The governor's split is executed; this half is fully supported today.

THE GAP, and its exact shape: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts:173-177 calls `buildInputManifest({baseIdentity: request.inputManifest.baseIdentity, entries: request.inputManifest.entries as never})`. It seals THE CALLER'S OWN ENTRIES — the `as never` cast is the tell. That is the accidental caller copy this task replaces with an observed one.

PRODUCERS, all reachable from the BARE @moe/runner root: `createNodeGitObserver` (index.ts:55), `createNodeScopePaths` (:56), `observeScope` (:59), `WorkspaceInputManifest` (:274), `buildInputManifest` (:279). Note :56 — `createNodeScopePaths` is exported and is the real `ScopePathObserver` implementation (scope-git.ts:223), so the daemon needs no filesystem fake for the accepted control.

THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE THAT SHAPES THE MODULE: `observeScope` returns `ScopeObservation` whose `canonicalEntries` are `ScopeCanonicalEntry = {path, attribution, attributionReason}` (scope-contract.ts:143-147). `ScopePathObserver` is `{realpath, exists}` (:76-79). So the hydrator's own work is exactly: observe -> read each observed path's raw bytes -> digest -> attach producer -> seal. There is no existing runner surface that does the middle step (`grep -n 'sha256|digest|Content' packages/runner/src/index.ts` returns nothing).

PRODUCER IDENTITY IS MANDATORY and the contract says why: `WorkspaceProducer` is `{kind:"BASE"}` | `{kind:"PREDECESSOR", attemptRef, epoch, adoptionRef?}` (workspace-contract.ts:50-57), with the comment "a content digest is one-way, so nothing downstream can ask 'which attempt produced these bytes' unless the input manifest already says". CONTRACT KEYS, re-verified: `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_INPUT_KEYS` = `["baseIdentity","entries"]` (foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:90). The AUTHORITY-FREE comment at :91-96 lists what is absent by construction — grant, effect, attempt, claim, priorRegistration, duplicateDelivery, wrapperIdentity, reconciliation, freshly observed runtime — and this producer must preserve that property.

THE NESTED-EXPORT TRAP, from worker-a83aecdf and worth keeping: `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` (claude-host-runtime.ts:201) and `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` reach the bare root through NESTED `export *` (index.ts -> surface/claude-surface.js -> claude-discovery-surface.js). planningNotes.risks:
1) THE CALLER-ECHO FAILURE IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES A GREEN SUITE. If the hydrator ends up sealing the request's entries under a new name, every test that only checks "a manifest came back" still passes. The defence is the positive assertion — caller entries that CONTRADICT disk, and the observed ones must win — plus drill #1. A reviewer should look for that test first.

2) DRILL #2 ONLY BITES IF A MISMATCHING BASE CASE EXISTS. Sealing against the proposal instead of the observation is invisible whenever the two agree, which is the happy path. Confirm a deliberate mismatch case exists before trusting the drill.

3) REAL GIT IN TESTS IS FRAGILE ON WINDOWS. `git init` in a temp dir inherits global config; pin `-c` settings, avoid signing, and close/remove every worktree in a `finally`. A leaked git process reads as an unrelated worker crash.
